heroSummary: For 2028–29, K–12 students in Denver Public Schools start school Monday, August 21. Early Childhood Education students start Tuesday, August 22. The last day of school is Friday, June 1, with a half-day early release. Thanksgiving Break runs November 20–24, Winter Break runs December 18–January 2, and Spring Break runs March 26–30. These are districtwide dates from the DPS family and student calendar. Individual schools may publish additional dates for testing, conferences, athletics, transportation changes, bell schedules, and other school events.
calendarNotes: DPS’s 2028–29 family and student calendar keeps the same key distinction used in the prior future-year calendar: K–12 and ECE start on different days, and observance dates are not automatically no-class days unless marked separately.

sourceReviewSummary: This page is based on the DPS calendars page and the official 2028–29 family and student calendar PDF.
sourceReviewDetails: August 4, 2026 — All districtwide dates on this page were checked against the DPS calendar page and the official PDF created May 19, 2026.

We checked the K–12 first day, ECE first day, last day, instructional-day count, holidays and no-class days, vacation and staff learning dates with no classes, holidays shown after the last student day, and the major break ranges.
The DPS PDF lists 174.5 instructional days.
Because this is a future-year calendar, the page will be reviewed again if DPS replaces the PDF or revises its calendar page.

calendarFaqs.q: Do ECE students start on the same day as K–12 students?
calendarFaqs.a: No. K–12 students start Monday, August 21, 2028. Early Childhood Education students start Tuesday, August 22.

calendarFaqs.q: Is January 2 part of Winter Break?
calendarFaqs.a: Yes. Winter Break runs through Tuesday, January 2, 2029. Students return Wednesday, January 3.

calendarFaqs.q: Does every DPS holiday or observance mean school is closed?
calendarFaqs.a: No. On the official DPS calendar, some dates are marked as holidays or observances even when school remains open. Look for a separate no-classes designation before assuming students are off.

calendarFaqs.q: Can the 2028–29 DPS calendar still change?
calendarFaqs.a: Yes. DPS currently publishes this as its 2028–29 family and student calendar, but the district may revise future-year dates. Check the official calendar page before making final plans.

calendarFaqs.q: Does the downloaded DPS calendar update automatically?
calendarFaqs.a: The .ics file is a one-time import, not a live calendar subscription. Download a new copy if DPS publishes a revised calendar.

calendarFaqs.q: Does this calendar include school-specific events?
calendarFaqs.a: This page covers districtwide dates only. Individual schools may publish separate dates for testing, conferences, athletics, transportation changes, bell schedules, and same-day announcements.

customSections.label: How to Read the DPS Calendar
customSections.content: The 2028–29 DPS calendar uses one marking for both vacation days and staff learning days when students do not have classes. It also uses separate markings for holidays, observances, first days, and the last day of school.

rows: K–12 students start August 21. ECE students start August 22.
Vacation or Staff Learning / No Classes
The same marking is used for vacation periods and some staff learning days. Students do not attend classes.
School may remain open unless the date is also marked no classes.
Students are released after the first half of the day.
